$comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the code-quality gate thresholds added alongside
the per-file coverage ratchet. Protected by scripts/gate-integrity.ts:
a PR may raise these numbers, never lower them (crapMaxScore is inverted —
lower is stricter — so it may only DECREASE). A maintainer-only
`gate-change-approved` label is the sole bypass.
Per-file coverage thresholds stay in scripts/coverage-thresholds.json —
that ratchet predates this file and owns ~500 keys. This file holds only
the NEW aggregate gates. See docs/features/platform/dev-lifecycle-and-gates.md.
Aggregate line-coverage floor across the merged coverage/lcov.info.
Complements (does NOT replace) the per-file ratchet: per-file catches a
single bad module, this catches slow drift across the whole tree.
CRAP = comp^2 * (1 - cov)^3 + comp, per function (McCabe cyclomatic
complexity x line coverage). A function at 100% coverage scores exactly
its complexity, so maxScore 30 means: complexity <=5 needs no coverage,
complexity >30 can never pass however well tested. 30 is the value from
the original Crap4J paper and every tool that followed it.
enforceGlobs scopes the gate to files the merged lcov actually measures.
warnScore only colours the report; it never fails a run.
TWO MODES, because a mature tree cannot adopt CRAP 30 in one commit:
--changed (PR gate)  every function the PR TOUCHED must be <= maxScore.
full repo (nightly)  a RATCHET on the existing debt — the violation
count may fall, never rise. maxFullRepoViolations
was 83 of 9505 scored functions, measured on main
2026-09-13 (40 of them complexity-only, already
at 100% coverage — only a refactor moves those).
Lower it as the debt is paid; gate-integrity.ts
refuses to raise it.
That 83 was measured WITHOUT the browser-route
coverage leg, which needs a CI-only receipt
(BROWSER_COVERAGE_RAW/LCOV) and cannot run
locally. Missing coverage only ever INFLATES a
CRAP score, so the real CI count is <= 83 and
this ceiling cannot false-fail. Ratchet it down
to the true number after the first nightly.
Stryker runs on the vitest leg only — it has no Bun test runner, and the
backend pool's per-file mock.module() isolation fights perTest coverage.
See docs/development-lifecycle.md -> 'Roadmap: mutation testing'.
scoreThreshold fails the run (Stryker thresholds.break). PR runs are
diff-scoped; the nightly workflow runs mutateGlobs in full.
prBudgetMinutes caps a PR run so a large diff cannot stall the queue.
WHY src/lib/server/** IS EXCLUDED — a sandbox limit, not a policy choice.
Stryker copies the project into web/.stryker-tmp/sandbox-*/ and runs the
tests there. web/vitest.config.ts aliases $server to resolve(__dirname,
'../src') — the REPO-ROOT src/ tree, which sits outside web/ and so is
never copied into the sandbox. Every *.server.test.ts therefore dies with
'Failed to resolve import "$server/..."' and Stryker aborts the whole run
on a failed initial test run. Measured: the 81-file scope failed outright;
dropping these 13 modules gives a valid 68-file scope (dry run green,
2617 tests). Validate any scope change cheaply with
`bun scripts/mutation.ts --full --dry-run-only` before paying for a run.
Lifting this needs the sandbox to contain repo-root src/ — i.e. running
Stryker from the repo root, or inPlace mode (which mutates the real
working tree and is unsafe on a box with concurrent agents).
